newsitem.title: INDIA: India Cements to rebid for cement unit.
newsitem.headline: India Cements to rebid for cement unit.

text.p: India Cements Ltd will bid again for state-run Cement Corporation of India's (CCI) cement unit in southern India, a company official said on Monday.
"We will bid again," T.V.Swaminathan, India Cements' general manager (operations) told Reuters on phone from Madras. India Cements had bid for CCI's plant at Yerraguntla last year.
The CCI on the weekend invited global bids for sale or joint venture of the Yerraguntla plant. It said SBI Capital Markets Ltd had been appointed to obtain, evaluate and recommend proposals.

CCI said it planned to sell 26 percent, 50 percent or 74 percent of ownership. The Yerraguntla plant has an installed capacity of 0.4 million tonnes of cement a year, with a scope to expand upto one million tonnes.
The existing plant and expansion are based on dry process of technology. The plant is located on a 1,126-acre plot in Cuddappah district of Andhra Pradesh.
The Yerraguntla unit produced 235,000 tonnes of cement in 1995/96 (April-March), CCI said.
India Cements had obtained government approval for a $50 million global depository receipts (GDR) issue to part finance acquisition of the Yerraguntla plant.
Jardine Fleming Broking (India) was appointed lead manager of the GDR issue which was not pursued.
India Cements' Swaminathan said CCI might have decided to invite fresh bids because there were only two contenders at last year's bidding.

Another reason could be that after last year's bid, the Yerraguntla unit was referred to the Bureau of Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR), the Indian agency engaged in rehibilitation of loss-making companies, he said.
The Yerraguntla unit is very close to India Cements' own plant at Chilamkur in Andhra Pradesh.
Part of the Sankar Group, India Cements is the largest cement manufacturer in South India with installed capacity of 2.6 million tonnes.
